Typhoon Dujuan Hits Japan, Causing Fatalities and Disruptions

Typhoon Dujuan made landfall in Japan, bringing heavy rains and strong winds that led to flood and landslide warnings. The storm caused at least five deaths and left six people missing, according to various reports. Approximately 45,000 homes experienced power outages, and two prefectures, Kanagawa and Chiba, were heavily impacted. The typhoon also led to the cancellation of flights and prompted evacuations, with one report stating 1.5 million people were urged to evacuate. The equestrian eventing competition at the Asian Games in Aichi Prefecture was postponed until Tuesday due to the approaching typhoon. The storm brought record rain to some areas.
